post.description:
Create a backup of the whole project of the user.\
\
The backup contains the project with its quota, the secrets and public-keys, the images and\
snapshots, the networks, virtual_machines, packet-filters and floating ip-addresses and a copy of\
the root-disk of every virtual_machine. Users and their assignments to the project are not part\
of it.\
\
The backup is created by a job in the background, which can be followed over the returned job.\
The project is locked for the whole duration of the backup, so all resources of the project can\
only be read in the meantime. A project, which is already locked by another backup or restore, is\
rejected with `409`.\
\
With `stop_vms` every running virtual_machine is shut down, while its root-disk is saved, and\
started again afterwards. Otherwise the virtual_machines are only paused shortly. With\
`include_images` the files of the images of the project are copied into the backup as well.\
\
The backup is encrypted with a key, which is derived from the `passphrase`. The passphrase is not\
stored, so the backup can't be restored without it.

get.description:
List the backups on a backup-target, which are not known yet.\
\
These are backups, which were copied onto the backup-target from outside, for example from\
another deployment for a disaster-recovery. Only complete backups with a manifest are listed. They\
can be imported with `POST /v1alpha/backup/import/admin`. This can only be done by an admin.

post.description:
Import a backup, which was copied onto a backup-target from outside, for example\
from another deployment for a disaster-recovery.\
\
The passphrase is checked against the manifest of the backup, before the backup is registered, so\
a wrong passphrase is rejected with `400`. Afterwards the backup belongs to the project, which it\
was created from, and can be restored like every other backup, also into a new project. The users\
of the old deployment are not part of the backup and have to be created and assigned to the\
restored project by an admin. This can only be done by an admin.

post.description:
Create a backup of a single virtual_machine of the project of the user.\
\
The backup contains the root-disk of the virtual_machine, its config, its public-key, its\
packet-filters, its floating ip-addresses and its network, which is created again on a restore,\
if it doesn't exist anymore.\
\
The backup is created by a job in the background, which can be followed over the returned job.\
The whole project is locked, while the root-disk is saved, because the backup also contains\
resources of the project, like the network. A project, which is already locked by another backup\
or restore, is rejected with `409`.\
\
With `stop_vm` the virtual_machine is shut down, while its root-disk is saved, and started again\
afterwards, if it was running. Otherwise it is only paused shortly.\
\
The backup is encrypted with a key, which is derived from the `passphrase`. The passphrase is not\
stored, so the backup can't be restored without it.

get.description:
Get a backup of the project of the user.\
\
The backup-target and the size of the backup are read from ryokan, which stores the files of the\
backup. They are empty, if ryokan doesn't know the backup or is not reachable.

delete.description:
Delete a backup together with its files and the secrets of its disks.\
\
Only admins of the project can delete a backup. A backup, which is created or restored right now,\
is rejected with `409`. If the deletion fails, the backup stays in the state `DELETING` and the\
deletion can be repeated.\
\
The project of a backup, whose creation was interrupted by a restart of isekai, is unlocked again\
by the deletion.

post.description:
Restore a backup into a project.\
\
The passphrase is checked against the manifest of the backup and its metadata is read, before\
anything is changed, so a wrong passphrase or a manipulated metadata-file is rejected with `400`.\
Afterwards the plan of the restore is calculated: which resources keep their UUID, which get a\
new one (`id_map`), which are overwritten and which are deleted by `prune`, and how the quota of\
the project is used afterwards. With `dry_run` only the plan is returned\
and nothing is changed. A restore, which would exceed the quota, is rejected with `409`.\
\
Then the project is locked and the backup is restored by a job in the background, which can be\
followed over the returned job. A project, which is already locked by another backup or restore,\
is rejected with `409`. The job checks the disks and images of the backup against its manifest,\
before it changes the project, so a manipulated backup changes nothing.\
\
- Without `force` a resource keeps its UUID, if it is free. A resource, whose UUID is used in\
  the project, gets a new one. Restored into another project, all resources get new UUIDs,\
  because their UUIDs are still used by the project of the backup.\
- With `force` every UUID is kept and existing resources are overwritten. A virtual_machine gets\
  the root-disk of the backup, or is created again, if its disk-size changed.\
- With `prune`, which is only allowed together with `force`, the resources of the project, which\
  are not part of the backup, are deleted, so the project gets exactly the state of the backup.\
- Floating ip-addresses are always allocated again. The virtual_machines get their power-state\
  from the time of the backup, or are started with `start_vms`.\
\
A backup of a project is restored into its own project, or into `target_project_id`. A project,\
which doesn't exist, is created with the name and quota of the backup. Users and their\
assignments to the project are never restored. A backup of a virtual_machine is restored into the\
project of the token, or into `target_project_id`, which must exist. A missing public-key is\
restored from the backup and a missing network is created from the backup, if\
`include_dependencies` is set.\
\
If the restore fails after it has changed the project, the project stays locked. It is unlocked\
by repeating the restore of the same backup with `force`, which takes over the lock, or by an\
admin.\
\
Admins of the project can restore into their own project, all other projects, also new ones,\
can only be restored by admins.

Secret.description:
Wrapper around a string, which must not be leaked into logs or error-messages.

`Debug` and `Display` both print `***` instead of the content, so a secret stays hidden even when it is part of a bigger struct, which is logged as a whole. The content is only reachable through `reveal`, which makes every intended access visible at the call-site.
